doc.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Jazz lingo: 'channel' means the bridge
summary: Rose and Rowe recall Williams saying 'channel' for the bridge, and she values learning from experienced players.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well I suppose so, because he has so many years of experience in playing in a vast variety of settings. I think that’s what makes the playing more enjoyable, because he has such a diverse background and I’m relatively new at this.
I remember, when we had played together, and during one song he leaned over and he said “channel” to me. And for a minute I didn’t know what he was talking about.

Yeah, I actually, he had said that one time to me, he was discussing that, and I didn’t know either. But then we found out that it meant the bridge of the tune. But yeah I guess that could be a little bit confusing.
Yeah, you kind of just pretend—

You kind of, sort of hear where he’s going and then go on with it. But I find that it’s a lot more enjoyable and wonderful to play with players that have more of a background and more experience, because I learn more from that. So yeah there’s a lot of new things that I hear while I’m playing, but then again I’m learning from that also.
